comments.content: A complete override pair is funnelled through `ButtonDefaults.buttonColors(...)` for every variant, so for the `Outline` and `Text` variants the supplied container replaces the variant's transparent one. Concretely: an `Outline`/`Text` button with fixed colours renders as a filled button, and while disabled it receives the *filled* disabled container (onSurface @ 12%) instead of the transparent container those variants normally use (`outlinedButtonColors()`/`textButtonColors()` set `disabledContainerColor = Color.Transparent`). That contradicts the documented intent that a Text button stays a text button. Consider deriving the override from the variant's own colour set (e.g. `filledTonalButtonColors(...)`, `outlinedButtonColors(...)`, `textButtonColors(...)` with the same `containerColor`/`contentColor`) so the variant semantics — in particular the disabled container — are preserved.
